items.title: Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer.
items.summary: Journal: Functional & integrative genomics. Abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterised by extensive genomic heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Although recurrent coding mutations in key driver genes have been well researched, large-scale sequencing studies have identified a broad array of non-coding variants which may contribute to tumorigenesis by interfering with gene regulatory mechanisms. However, understanding the functional significance of these variants remains a major challenge due to their abundance and the complexity of non-coding regulatory structures. This review outlines current computational and experimental techniques to identify, prioritise, and functionally validate non-coding variants in PDAC. We discuss in silico methods including genome-wide association study (GWAS) fine-mapping, colocalisation, machine learning-driven functional annotation, and the use of established computational tools, in addition to epigenomic profiling technologies including, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, and CUT&RUN which define regulatory landscapes. We also emphasise new AI-based methods involving radiogenomics, AI imaging analysis and data integration, which provides novel potential to link genomic variation with phenotypic and imaging characteristics. Additionally, we highlight experimental validation techniques including reporter assays, electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSA), chromatin conformation capture methods, and CRISPR-based perturbation systems used to study variant functionality. Together, these complementary approaches establish a framework for correlating non-coding variation to regulatory mechanisms in PDAC.
items.headline: Computational and experimental methods validate non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer
items.brief: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) harbors many non-coding genomic variants whose functional roles are unclear. This review outlines computational approaches like GWAS fine-mapping, colocalization, machine learning annotation, and epigenomic profiling (ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN) to identify regulatory variants. Experimental validations include reporter assays, EMSA, chromatin conformation capture, and CRISPR perturbations, establishing a framework to link non-coding variation to gene regulation in PDAC.
items.why: It advances understanding of non-coding regulatory variants in cancer genomics, relevant for interpreting regulatory elements and integrating epigenomic data.
items.korean: 췌장암에서 비암호화 변이의 기능적 중요성을 계산 및 실험적으로 검증하는 방법을 제시합니다.

items.title: Artificial intelligence aids multi-omics data integration in cancer drug discovery and development: from targets to drug synergy.
items.summary: Journal: Acta pharmacologica Sinica. Abstract: The emergence of multi-omics technologies has enabled the integration of genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data to characterize the molecular complexity of cancer. Single-cell and spatial profiling further resolve intratumoral heterogeneity, cell-cell interactions, and the microenvironmental determinants of therapeutic responses. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) provides computational approaches for integrating these heterogeneous data types across target identification, drug response prediction, toxicity assessment, and drug-combination modeling. Across these domains, the available evidence indicates that multi-omics integration is most beneficial when the included layers provide complementary biological information; that single-cell and spatial omics analyses reveal treatment-resistant populations and niches but remain largely research-grade and thus not ready for routine clinical deployment; and that although foundation models support some representation-learning tasks, their advantages in perturbation-response prediction require confirmation via stringent evaluation. By distinguishing externally validated advances from retrospective proof-of-concept studies, we provide a practical framework for evaluating the translational readiness of AI-driven multi-omics tools in precision oncology.
items.headline: AI integrates multi-omics data for cancer drug discovery and synergy prediction
items.brief: This study reviews AI methods for integrating genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data to characterize cancer complexity. It highlights single-cell and spatial profiling for resolving heterogeneity and microenvironment effects. AI aids target identification, drug response prediction, toxicity, and drug-combination modeling. The review distinguishes validated advances from proof-of-concept studies and provides a framework to assess translational readiness of AI-driven multi-omics tools in precision oncology.
items.why: It provides a comprehensive framework for AI-based multi-omics integration, crucial for computational genomics and epigenomics in cancer therapeutics.
items.korean: 암 다중오믹스 데이터를 AI로 통합해 약물 발견과 시너지 예측에 활용하는 방법을 제시합니다.

items.title: OCCAM: Improved Single-Cell Representation Learning and Perturbation Effect Prediction
items.summary: Predicting the effects of genetic perturbations requires models that generalize beyond observed cell contexts and gene combinations. We introduce Occam, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) framework for representation learning and perturbation-effect prediction. Occam combines cell representations learned through denoising with gene interaction, text, and protein-sequence features. It achieves the highest aggregate representation scores for perturbation information and cell-type preservation with batch integration. In cross-context few-shot prediction, a perturbation and a cell context are each observed during training, but never together. Occam better captures the measured response patterns for these unobserved combinations than four retrained competitors or direct transfer of the same perturbation's measured effects from other training cell lines. Without fine-tuning, Occam best distinguishes perturbations among the evaluated models and simple baselines in cell lines held out from predictor training, across seen and unseen assays. Predicting expression levels accurately in these settings remains challenging. For double perturbations, which target two genes simultaneously, Occam composes learned single-gene responses to better capture the combined response and reduce expression error compared with competing models and summed single-gene effects. These gains extend to both strongly additive and weakly additive responses. Together, these results support simple MLPs for cell representation learning and perturbation-effect prediction across contexts and gene combinations.
items.headline: Occam: MLP framework for cell representation and perturbation effect prediction
items.brief: Occam is a multilayer perceptron model combining denoised cell representations with gene interaction, text, and protein features to predict genetic perturbation effects. It excels in few-shot cross-context prediction where perturbation and cell context are seen separately but not jointly. Occam outperforms retrained competitors and direct transfer methods, better capturing combined double perturbation responses. These results support simple MLPs for generalizable cell representation learning and perturbation effect prediction.
items.why: It advances computational genomics by providing a robust, generalizable model for predicting gene perturbation effects across contexts, aiding biological foundation models.
items.korean: 세포 표현 학습과 유전자 교란 효과 예측에 강력한 MLP 기반 모델을 제안합니다.
items.evidence_note: Preprint status; predictive accuracy remains challenging for expression levels.

items.title: Modeling quantum information scrambling in realistic protein NMR experiments
items.summary: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are important probes of operator spreading and information scrambling, and have recently been proposed as a means of extracting molecular structural information through nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Realizing this potential requires accurate modeling of OTOCs in complex molecular environments within experimentally relevant settings. Here, we develop an end-to-end computational pipeline connecting molecular structures to OTOC dynamics in protein systems. Our framework incorporates molecular motion through molecular dynamics simulations, orientational averaging appropriate for powder samples, and spin-network truncation, using an experimentally realizable double-quantum effective Hamiltonian. We apply this framework to a dataset of over 350 carbon-carbon spin pairs across 10 protein systems, spanning interspin distances of 5-17 A. We find that OTOC arrival times scale approximately linearly with interspin distance, revealing system-dependent operator-spreading velocities that enable correlations to propagate over extended distances within milliseconds. Our sensitivity analysis further shows that individual OTOCs predominantly constrain a single structural parameter, primarily associated with interspin distance. Together, these findings highlight the potential of OTOCs to probe spatially extended spin correlations on timescales compatible with solid-state NMR experiments.
items.headline: Modeling quantum information scrambling in protein NMR experiments
items.brief: This work develops a computational pipeline linking protein molecular structures to out-of-time-order correlator (OTOC) dynamics measurable by NMR. Incorporating molecular dynamics, orientational averaging, and spin-network truncation, it analyzes over 350 carbon-carbon spin pairs across 10 proteins. OTOC arrival times scale linearly with interspin distance, revealing operator-spreading velocities enabling millisecond-scale correlations. Sensitivity analysis shows OTOCs constrain primarily interspin distances, highlighting their potential for probing spatially extended spin correlations in solid-state NMR.
items.why: It bridges quantum information concepts with experimental NMR, enabling computational genomics researchers to explore spatial chromatin and protein interaction dynamics.
items.korean: 단백질 NMR에서 양자 정보 스크램블링을 모델링해 공간적 상호작용을 정량화합니다.

items.title: Expressivity of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states
items.summary: Tensor network states (TNS) provide a family of efficiently compressed approximations to physically relevant many-body quantum states. An important quantity that characterizes the computational resources required by a TNS is its bond dimension. While in one dimension an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy guarantees an exact matrix product state representation with a bond dimension independent of the system size, an analogous statement does not hold for general states in two dimensions (2D). This leaves open the question of how the expressivity of 2D TNS is related to the entanglement properties of the states they represent. In this work, we focus on two families of 2D translation-invariant Gaussian fermionic states: single-band BCS superconductors and half-filled two-band insulators (including semimetals). For each family, we prove that an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy is equivalent to having an exact Gaussian fermionic TNS representation with a finite bond dimension determined by the Renyi-0 entropy. We also establish equivalent characterizations in terms of compactly supported Wannier-type orbitals and the momentum-space wavefunction, relating the spatial extent of these orbitals and the structure of the wavefunction to the required bond dimension.
items.headline: Expressivity of 2D Gaussian fermion tensor network states linked to entanglement area law
items.brief: This study proves that for 2D translation-invariant Gaussian fermionic states (single-band BCS superconductors and two-band insulators), an area law for Renyi-0 entropy is equivalent to exact finite bond dimension Gaussian fermionic tensor network state (TNS) representations. It relates spatially localized Wannier-type orbitals and momentum-space wavefunctions to required bond dimension, clarifying how entanglement properties govern TNS expressivity in two dimensions.
items.why: It provides rigorous connections between entanglement measures and tensor network representations, relevant for computational models of chromatin and regulatory element interactions.
items.korean: 2차원 가우시안 페르미온 텐서 네트워크 상태의 표현력과 엔탱글먼트 법칙의 등가성을 증명합니다.

items.headline: Montclair Art Museum to open exhibition on ‘Mad’ magazine artwork in February
items.brief: Montclair Art Museum announces an upcoming exhibition featuring artwork from ‘Mad’ magazine, highlighting its cultural and artistic significance. The exhibition opens in February and showcases original pieces that influenced American satire and visual art.
items.why: It offers a culturally rich perspective on visual art history, relevant for fine art enthusiasts interested in the evolution of satire and graphic art.
